script.title: Job vs Mass Production
script.caption_hook: Why is a custom suit costly but a readymade shirt cheap?

lines.say: Why is a custom suit costly but readymade shirts are cheap?
Great question! That's job production versus mass production.
So what exactly is job production, Ma'am?
A tailor stitches one suit per order. That's job. A readymade factory makes the same shirt in thousands. That's Mass.
So if nobody orders, the tailor doesn't stitch?
Exactly. No order, no production. Job is high variety, low volume. Mass is the opposite.
Hmm, what about machines and workers?
Job uses general-purpose machines and skilled labour. Mass uses special-purpose machines, so semi-skilled workers are enough.
Job uses a process layout, grouping similar machines. Mass uses a product layout, one fixed line.
Oh! So why is the shirt cheaper?
Mass spreads its cost over a large volume, so cost per unit is lower. Job costs more per unit.
Is batch production the same as job?
No. Batch makes a group of identical units at a time. It lies in between.
Remember: job is tailor-made, one order. Mass is readymade, standard, in bulk.

check_notes: Writer: Versus right_on "Mass" now appears as a word in line 4. Check total word count is within 120-175.

Checker: Line 12 (voice): 'Mass spreads its cost over a large volume' is imprecise. Only the fixed costs (special machines, tooling, set-up) get spread over the volume. Correct version: 'Mass production spreads its fixed costs over a very large volume and gains economies of scale, so cost per unit is lower.'

Checker: Lines 4 and 15 (example): many Operations Management texts give readymade garments as a standard example of batch production (sizes and designs are made in batches), not mass production. To keep the example clear, say 'the same shirt design made continuously in thousands on a fixed line', or use a standard mass production example such as cars, cement or sugar. This keeps Line 14's batch category distinct.
Checker: Line 4 (voice): 'That's Mass.' has a capital M that isn't needed. Correct version: 'That's mass production.'
